blocks.label: DDR5/DDR4 memory PHY: 10 x16 DQ units + 4 probable CA/CK units in two groups (2 MCs x 2 DDR5 sub-channels of 32+4 ECC bits, or 2 DDR4 channels of 64+8)
blocks.notes: Repeating PHY macros along the top edge, left 56% of the die. Bottom edge measured at the y=82 gutter (A had 101, which included the empty fill strip below it). The 13900K supports DDR5-5600 / DDR4-3200. audit2: the strip is [group A: DQx5 CAx2][common][group B: CAx2 DQx5] (children ddr_phy_a / ddr_phy_common / ddr_phy_b). The two groups are translated copies of the same macros (CA NCC 0.81 translated vs 0.35 mirrored); only the ORDER of unit types is mirrored, about x~1088.5 px. 160 physical DQ lanes (10 units x 16, inferred from Locuza's 128-bit + 32b ECC label); DDR5 bonds 144 of them (DDRn_DQ4[3:0] = 4 ECC bits per 32-bit sub-channel in Intel's ballout). Right edge 2140 -> 2141 (last trailing grid column ends at 2141-2142).

blocks.label: DDR PHY group A (DMI end): 5 x16 DQ units + 2 probable CA/CK units
blocks.notes: Geometry high, channel mapping medium-low. DQ units at x 35-685 (starts 35/165/295/425/555, pitch 130 px), CA-type units at 685-845 (outer) and 845-1003 (inner), trailing grid column 1003-1019 (every unit starts with that column; each group ends with one extra, so both groups are 984-985 px wide). Which sub-channels each group carries is NOT visible on silicon. Intel's LGA1700 ballout (743844, re-checked in research/audit2/orient/pins.json) orders the DDR lands along the edge as DQ[DDR0+DDR2] - CA[DDR0] - CA[DDR2] | CA[DDR3] - CA[DDR1] - DQ[DDR3+DDR1] (DDR5 names; DDR0/1 = MC0, DDR2/3 = MC1): palindromic like the die, with MC0's CA outermost. If the package keeps that order (crossing every byte of two sub-channels over the centre would be implausible), each die group carries ONE 32-bit sub-channel of EACH memory controller, the outer CA unit of each group is MC0's and the inner one MC1's, and with the flip-chip mirror group A (DMI end, package-south) carries DDR1+DDR3 and group B carries DDR0+DDR2. Confidence: medium-low. The app's wiring routes MC0 only to group A and MC1 only to group B; that is a drawing convention (see wiring.notes).

ring.notes: 14 ring stops: 8 P-core/LLC agents, 4 E-cluster/LLC agents, the System Agent end and the iGPU end. PHYSICAL: each P/E column of the ring band holds TWO mirror-image agents SIDE BY SIDE (measured left/right mirror symmetry; Locuza draws 'Ring Agent | Ring Agent' per column on ADL-S). Each stop's agent_rect is that half-block. LOGICAL: the coherent fabric is drawn as one flattened loop. The top track runs left to right through one agent per column, the bottom track returns right to left through the other. This gives the order SA -> P0..P3 -> E0, E1 -> iGPU -> E3, E2 -> P7..P4 -> SA. TechPowerUp's die-shot reading supports that pattern (half the P-cores, half the E-clusters, iGPU, the other E-clusters, the other P-cores, uncore). Assigning top-row cores to the top track and to the left agent of each pair is a convention, not an observation. Ring wires are not visible on a poly-layer shot. Both directions of the ring pass every stop; the loop shape is schematic. The track y values are schematic, at the quarter points of the band. audit2: Since Tiger Lake, Intel's client coherent fabric is a dual ring: two independent 32-byte-wide rings; every agent (each core/LLC ring agent, the GT and the uncore/SA) has one ring stop on each ring and can use either (Intel Hot Chips 32 Tiger Lake: 'Dual ring microarchitecture'). Alder Lake kept the dual ring (1000 GB/s), and one ring can be powered down at low load. Raptor Lake-S is assumed to inherit it; no Raptor-Lake-specific source was found. On the GT side gpu_global holds two GTI ports (Locuza ADL-P: 'Global Assets (GAM, 2x GTI)'). The single loop drawn stands for both rings; which silicon belongs to which ring is not visible on a poly-layer shot. Stop markers now sit at the centre of each agent's inner L3-control/ring-stop block (Nemez), not at the half-column centre (the tag/control seam).

wiring.notes: Schematic of logical paths through physical channels: the wires themselves are in metal layers a poly-layer photo can't show. Cores drop through their LLC slice/CBo to their ring agent; the SA reaches MC0/MC1 through the memory fabric and each MC its own half of the DDR PHY; the I/O fabric runs from the SA to the PCIe/DMI controller column. Measured and argued in research/audit2/interconnect/wiring.json. v2: the 24 core / LLC / E-gutter nodes follow the ring-stop markers, which moved to the centre of each agent's L3-control/ring-stop block (Nemez), so every core -> LLC -> stop drop stays axis-aligned; the memory-fabric line moved from y 596 to 609.5 (the IMC lower group imc_shared now ends at 602, the SA starts at 617). DDR: the app sends MC0 only to PHY group A and MC1 only to group B. That is a drawing convention: Intel's ballout land order (palindromic CA[MC0] CA[MC1] | CA[MC1] CA[MC0]) suggests each group carries one 32-bit sub-channel of EACH controller, so in silicon both channels' lanes span both groups. The strip y 82-115 under the PHY is featureless fill on the poly layer; the PHY-to-MC wires are not visible.
